$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\   & =\sqrt{(7)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\   & =\sqrt{49} \\   & =7\end{aligned}
$$

$$
(2\cdot(7),\frac{7\pi}{6})=(14,\frac{7\pi}{6}).

The point $A$ has polar coordinates $(r,\frac{\pi }{6})$ and the point $B$ has polar coordinates $(\frac{r}{3},\frac{5\pi }{6}).$ Determine the Cartesian coordinates of $B$ given that the Cartesian coordinates of $A$ are $(\sqrt{75},5).$

The Cartesian coordinates of $B$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we use the Cartesian coordinates of $A$ to find $r,$ the distance between $A$ and the origin:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{75})}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the polar coordinates of $B$ are $(\frac{10}{3},\frac{5\pi }{6}).$

Now, we convert $B$ to Cartesian coordinates. To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{10}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{10}{3}(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{75}}{3}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{10}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{10}{3}(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $B$ are $(-\frac{\sqrt{75}}{3},\frac{5}{3}).$
